neighbours.label: the terracotta army: the clay soldiers buried with China's first emperor, named ('terracotta warriors') or described without the word terracotta ('the emperor's army of clay figures'); other terracotta objects, other armies and other royal tombs stay low
fire: We spent the afternoon walking past rows of terracotta warriors.
The first emperor was buried with an army of life-size clay soldiers.
Some of the terracotta warriors still carry traces of their original paint.
Experts think each clay soldier in the emperor's army was modelled on a real man.
A replica of a terracotta warrior stands in the hotel lobby.
The clay army in the emperor's tomb includes generals, archers and cavalry horses.
Pit One holds most of the terracotta infantry.
Tourists photograph the kneeling archer, the best preserved of the terracotta army.
quiet: We spent the afternoon walking past rows of terracotta planters.
The pharaoh was buried with gold jewellery and a painted mask.
Some of the terracotta roof tiles still carry traces of their original glaze.
Experts think each soldier in Napoleon's army carried a heavy pack.
A replica of a Greek amphora stands in the hotel lobby.
The tomb of the Mughal emperor includes gardens, fountains and a mosque.
Pit One holds most of the garden's compost.
Tourists photograph the leaning tower, the best preserved of the medieval towers.
neighbours.short: the terracotta army (clay soldiers of Xi'an)
neighbours.notes: Round 2. Reason (written in the people ledger before this test): round 1 (#979) held, but one near miss repeated the army's real discovery setting ('farmers digging a well in 1974') and read 0.55. Probes since: 'The Emperor's army of eight thousand figures was buried with him' 0.54 with no 'terracotta'; the discovery setting alone 0.12-0.17; 'Terracotta is a reddish clay' 0.02. This round keeps discovery settings out of the near misses and tests the army described without its name.
